newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Campbell Soup sets stock buyback.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Campbell Soup sets stock buyback.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co, in a plan it says will create earnings per share growth outpacing the food industry, said it would tender for up to $1.5 billion of its shares and divest several non-strategic businesses. The company also is acquiring Erasco Group, Germany's leading canned soup company, for $210 million.

CAMDEN, N.J., Sept. 5 -- Campbell Soup Company (NYSE: CPB) today announced a set of strategic actions to accelerate its sales and earnings per share growth to fulfill the company's vision of "Best in Show." Those actions include a $1.5 billion one-time stock repurchase, and the acquisition of the Erasco Group, the leading canned soup company in Germany, which ranks as the largest commercial soup market outside the U.S.

"We are poised for breaking away from our competitors in the food industry," David W. Johnson, Campbell Chairman, President, and Chief Executive Officer said. "This strategic growth plan is designed to vault our company into the ranks of the world's renowned consumer goods companies, in terms of financial profile and market multiple.

"Now, more than ever, our vision is within reach," said Johnson, unveiling the plan in a meeting with securities analysts in New York City. "Our confidence springs from a track record of accomplishments which has moved Campbell to the top of the fiercely competitive food industry. Our 1996 results, the sixth consecutive year of record sales and earnings, demonstrate that we are well positioned for this ambitious growth plan. Armed with our powerhouse brands, we are moving forward with a full-scale strategic growth plan."

Funding for the company's investments in growth, Johnson said, will come from a combination of key initiatives. The Company plans the divestiture of several non-strategic businesses with sales of approximately $500 million over the next two years. It will also undertake a refocusing and sale of various plant operations, as well as a number of targeted reductions in administrative and operational staff functions. These moves will result in a first quarter 1997 after-tax charge of approximately $160 million and will result in savings of $200 million over the next two years.

A number of brand innovations and investments will lead the growth plan, according to Johnson. They include: new line of premium-quality Campbell's ready-to-serve soups; faster rollout of the Franco American Superiore range of premium canned pasta products; a new range of Campbell's frozen soups; Swanson Broth in resealable cartons. Also, Pace Mexican sauces are being launched in Germany; a new joint venture was announced for retail sales of Godiva Chocolates in Japan; and a major new nutritionally balanced food program from Campbell's Center for Nutrition and Wellness will soon move into test phase.
In addition, Campbell announced plans to increase its advertising spending substantially, mainly for U.S. soup, Pepperidge Farm Goldfish, V-8 and Swanson frozen foods.

The Erasco acquisition, Johnson said, "provides us with a valuable platform in terms of heat-processed manufacturing, distribution, marketing and brand strength. Together with other businesses, Erasco will accelerate our growth throughout Germany and across the European Union." Campbell is purchasing Erasco from Grand Metropolitan for approximately US$210 million.

Johnson outlined how the Company's strategic growth plan is intended to increase earnings per share growth at a rate above the food industry. One dramatic element, Johnson said, was the Campbell Board of Directors authorization for stock repurchases of up to $2.5 billion. The buyback will be accomplished through a "dutch auction" one-time tender offer for up to $1.5 billion, followed by a ramped-up open market purchase program. The company will announce the details of the "dutch auction" next week.

"We are determined to build on our excellent record of creating shareowner wealth," Johnson said. "For Fiscal 1996, Campbell's total return to shareowners was 47 percent. Over the last six years, our total return has grown at more than 19 percent annually, outpacing both the S&P 500 (13%) and the S&P Food Group (12%). This is Best in Class' performance. Now it is time for Best in Show.'" SOURCE Campbell Soup Company
